result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A ties its four steps directly to placing a first purchase order. It moves team, approvals, accounting and cycle counts into an 'After your first order' section and briefly explains why each can wait. B also cuts the feature list and adds a useful reordering insight, but it still shows all nine numbered steps, keeps approvals and team setup near the front, and says less about when deferred items come back. B also uses awkward wording like 'about 4 steps.' | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B ties setup to one clear goal: four steps to a first purchase order. It moves team, approvals, accounting and cycle counts to an 'After your first order' group and briefly says why each can wait. A cuts the feature list well and catches that par levels were set before items were imported, but it still shows all nine steps in a three-tier checklist, and approval rules sit in the middle tier instead of being deferred. Both make assumptions about the product (A a spreadsheet template, B a par-level column and an example count of 212 items), and both say these need checking.
